label: Testing whether an actual missing perfection separates limited and unlimited degrees
summary: A missing genuine item plus preservation strictly orders profiles by inclusion. On a scalar least-upper-bound calibration, even if the source attains a highest level omitted by the recipient, cofinal recipient levels can give a tie. The exact criterion under inclusion is a realized giver level not bounded by the recipient degree. The new registered 1fd78e87 derives existing 8176a284 for actual identity-giver pairs when every actual recipient level is bounded by its nature's capacity and the same giver possesses an admitted pure item at a level strictly above that capacity, using common calibration and the existing degree-to-more bridge. Inclusion is unnecessary on this crossing route. It supplies a support option for the common-source maximal causality argument, while f2ca811c uses the universal fd2c8710 at each nonprimary bearer and the primary. In the prior substantive mode contrast 94271978, own-being versus receipt can motivate an additional constitutive perfection, but cannot calibrate it. Actual self-understanding has an independent conditional source-side route through immateriality, pure exercise and immanent primary self-form. Under defended purity and preservation it could separate the source profile from a noncognitive recipient, but it supplies no scalar ceiling on the recipient's remaining actualities, and does not distinguish all reflective recipients. See docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md, section 'When does a missing perfection make a bearer strictly less?', and Scratch/strict-esse-scale/Comparison.lean.
blocker: A positive crossing for every eligible actual source-recipient pair and the universal comparison each remain open. Evaluate a reflective recipient as the next hard case: compare the positive content each bearer actually grasps about the grounds of its own present actuality. Then test whether any difference orders complete profiles or crosses an independently justified ceiling in esse. A general grade assignment that depends on the desired source rank cannot supply that justification.
